item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.20)] Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), What Is Behind The Fresh Attention?
item.description:

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.22)] Rosenblatt initiates Alphabet stock coverage with buy rating on cloud By Investing.com
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.22)
Rosenblatt has initiated coverage on Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) with a "buy" rating and a price target of $410, citing the company's strong position in AI infrastructure and its cloud growth momentum. The firm believes that concerns about search have largely been addressed and that Alphabet is poised for multiple expansion as operating profits in cloud computing scale beyond current expectations. This optimism is tempered by the acknowledgment that a deceleration in cloud growth would pose a greater risk than new search competition.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.03)] CoStar Group (CSGP) Stock Looks Undervalued Despite Mixed Valuation Signals
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.03)
CoStar Group (CSGP) stock has declined significantly over the past year, leading to an estimated intrinsic value of $63 per share based on a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model, suggesting it is currently undervalued by about 46.7%. However, broader valuation checks, including a P/S ratio of 3.8x which is higher than the industry average, indicate a mixed picture rather than a clear bargain. The article concludes that the key question is whether CoStar Group can achieve the free cash flow levels assumed by the intrinsic value model, making the current discount either compensation for risks or a genuine opportunity.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.30)] Analog Devices Earnings: Raising Fair Value Estimate with AI Strength
item.description:

The company reported fiscal third-quarter revenue above guidance and expects continued strong growth, with its high-quality analog business well-positioned to benefit from AI trends. item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.15)] Apple Removes Kromix AI App Over Sexualized Deepfake Concerns
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.15)
Apple has removed the AI image-editing app Kromix from its App Store due to its ability to generate sexualized deepfakes of real individuals. This action follows a Meta advertising campaign for Kromix that used a deepfake resembling a U.S. female politician, promoting the app with "no restrictions" to male users. Apple reinforced its App Review Guidelines, which forbid apps creating or distributing pornography, including "nudification" tools, and also removed MaskAI for similar violations.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.28)] Nvidia Reportedly Explores Stake in AI Data Provider Mercor At $20B Valuation
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.28)
Nvidia is reportedly exploring an investment in the AI data-labeling startup Mercor, which would value the three-year-old firm at $20 billion in a new funding round. This potential deal highlights Nvidia's increasing focus on open-source AI capabilities and its aggressive venture capital deployment, having paid Mercor millions last quarter for specialized human-expert data for its Nemotron models. The investment would build upon Mercor's significant growth, with its annualized gross revenue reaching $2 billion in June.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.33)] Marvell: With Google Chip Deal, Firm Landing the White Whale
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.33)
Marvell Technology Inc. has secured a commercial agreement with Google for custom chips, including AI inference accelerators, which significantly expands Marvell's long-term AI growth potential. This deal, involving warrants for up to 7% of Marvell's shares if Google spends $120 billion by fiscal 2033, has led Morningstar to raise its fair value estimate for Marvell stock to $270 per share from $235. The firm views this as a strong endorsement of Marvell's custom silicon strategy and anticipates more details during Marvell's upcoming July-quarter results report.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.27)] AppLovin vs. Kratos Defense: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.27)
This article compares AppLovin (APP) and Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (KTOS) as technology stock investments for 2026, highlighting their different business models, financial performance, and risk profiles. AppLovin specializes in AI-driven ad tech with high margins and strong cash flow, while Kratos focuses on defense hardware, benefiting from government contracts. Despite AppLovin's faster growth, the author recommends Kratos for long-term growth due to its reliable government client and the increasing demand for its defense technologies in a geopolitically unstable environment.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.21)] News | Why big investors are buying Seattle apartments again
item.description:

Recent record-breaking sales, such as BGO's $500 million acquisition of two properties, suggest investors believe apartment values have bottomed out and are betting on future growth driven by factors like the AI and tech boom. While recovery is selective, focusing on newer, transit-oriented properties, the overall trend indicates a bullish outlook for Seattle's multifamily sector.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.10), NVDA Neutral (+0.13)] Is ServiceNow (NOW) Quietly Becoming the Default Orchestrator for Enterprise AI Automation?

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.44), MSFT Bullish (+0.21), AMZN Bullish (+0.24)] Apple stock stands out among Magnificent Seven on low AI spending
item.category: AAPL Bullish (+0.44), MSFT Bullish (+0.21), AMZN Bullish (+0.24)
item.description:

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.15)] SEC's "Reg Crypto" Lays Groundwork for Token-Based Fundraising
item.description:

The SEC has proposed "Reg Crypto," a new set of rules designed to facilitate token-based fundraising for entrepreneurs on blockchain infrastructure. This move aims to provide a clear regulatory path for capital formation through newly issued tokens, addressing previous ambiguities that pushed such activities overseas. The new guidelines are expected to stimulate issuance activity in the US, driving value to underlying blockchains like Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.35)] Microsoft signs offtake deal for wastewater-based carbon removal
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.35)
Microsoft has entered into an offtake agreement with climate tech startup Crew Carbon for wastewater-based carbon removal. Crew Carbon's technology, developed at Yale, enhances wastewater alkalinity to permanently remove carbon dioxide emitted by wastewater treatment plants by converting biogenic CO2 into stable bicarbonate ions. This deal is part of Microsoft's ongoing carbon removal efforts, despite previous reports of a pause in their CDR purchases.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.22), MSFT Bearish (-0.25)] Google’s founders didn’t market test Alphabet’s name before launching the now $1.9 trillion juggernaut. Here's the advice Steve Jobs gave Larry Page
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.22), MSFT Bearish (-0.25)
The article discusses how Google's founders, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, did not market test the name "Alphabet" for their parent company, despite its eventual $1.9 trillion valuation. It highlights advice Steve Jobs gave Larry Page in 2011 about focusing on a few key products, a philosophy Page initially adopted but later diverged from with Alphabet's broader vision. The piece also details Page and Brin's current net worth and their roles in Alphabet.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.44)] Apple ended support early for five Apple Watch models, new class action alleges
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.44)
A new class action lawsuit has been filed against Apple Inc. alleging that the company prematurely ended software support for five Apple Watch models, including the Series 6, 7, 8, SE (2nd generation), and Ultra. The lawsuit claims Apple sold these devices for up to $799 without disclosing the limited software support, causing consumers to be stuck with potentially buggy or slow devices. Plaintiff Richard Goetz seeks compensatory and punitive damages, restitution, and injunctive relief, claiming breach of contract and violation of California's Unfair Competition Law.

The set also comes with 12 Nano Metalfigs and an interactive "Duke" controller that unlocks lighting effects and in-game soundtracks.
